- `qname` is a `string dns_label` with `child_length = 0` (variable length), so `child_length = end - p` (all remaining data)
- `decode_value` is called with `data = p` (qname position) and `data_len = child_length = end - p`

So in `decode_dns_labels`, `data = p` (qname position) and `data_len = end - p` (remaining bytes in the packet from qname).

Then `buf_len = data + data_len - packet = p + (end - p) - packet = end - packet = packet_len`.

And `end_buf = buf + buf_len = data + packet_len = p + packet_len`.

The actual buffer end is `packet + packet_len`. Since `p >= packet + 12`, `end_buf >= packet + 12 + packet_len`, which is at least 12 bytes past the actual buffer end.

So the OOB read can happen when the label length byte at position `p` causes reads past `packet + packet_len`.

where `end = data + packet_len = p + packet_len`.

So `*p <= packet_len - 1` for the check to pass.

The label data is read from `p+1` to `p+1+*p`. The actual buffer end is `packet + packet_len`. So the read is OOB if `p + 1 + *p > packet + packet_len`, i.e., `*p > packet + packet_len - p - 1`.

Since `p = packet + 12` for the first question's qname, we need `*p > packet_len - 13`, i.e., `*p >= packet_len - 12`.
